summary: Intermittent RBAC authorization failures in Private VPC when exchanging opaque ID tokens
description:
Issue summary: Customers on private VPC deployment (CloudCart) see intermittent 403/401 responses from the Redwood gateway when using opaque ID tokens issued by the customer's IdP. Impact: Several API requests from the same user session succeed, then start failing for ~5-15 minutes before recovering without configuration changes. Environment: Private deployment in us-east region behind customer-managed ingress (ALB) with OIDC IdP and token introspection enabled.

Observed behavior follows the pattern: successful token exchange -> calls succeed -> after token refresh or periodic cache eviction, subsequent calls return 403 with message 'rbac: principal not found' or occasionally 401 'invalid token'. This began after a routine rotation of IdP signing keys on the customer side.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use CloudCart private VPC (prod-us-east) with IdP that issues opaque ID tokens and supports introspection.
2) Authenticate in client app to obtain an opaque ID token from the IdP.
3) Call Redwood private API endpoints through the customer's ALB using the opaque token in Authorization header.
4) Repeat calls over 30+ minutes while IdP performs background key rotations or token refreshes.
5) Observe intermittent 403/401 responses; successful calls interspersed with failures without changes to client or server config.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z gateway[auth] INFO received token: <opaque> for client_id=cloudcart-ui
2026-03-10T14:22:03Z rbac-service WARN lookup principal failed: subject=user:12345, reason=principal_lookup; cache_miss=true
2026-03-10T14:22:03Z gateway[auth] ERROR token-introspection 502 upstream error: remote introspection endpoint returned 5xx
2026-03-10T14:24:10Z gateway[auth] INFO token refresh detected for subject=user:12345, new_token=<opaque>
2026-03-10T14:24:10Z rbac-service ERROR evaluate policy failed: subject=user:12345, reason=unknown_claims
2026-03-10T14:27:05Z gateway[auth] INFO token cache eviction for subject=user:12345, reason=ttl_expired
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token introspection result changed shape after IdP key rotation and our RBAC mapping code treats missing claims as absent principal.
Found sequence where introspection returned 'active: true' but omitted 'sub' claim briefly during IdP rotation window; rbac-service requires sub or preferred_username to map to principal.
Timing correlation: customer confirmed IdP rotated signing keys at 2026-03-10T14:20Z; our logs show first errors at 14:22Z and intermittent recovery at 14:28Z.
Proxy layer (customer ALB) occasionally retries introspection requests, exposing a 502 from IdP; our retry path returns 401 downstream which the client sees as 'invalid token'.

Cache behavior: token/introspection cache TTL set to 30s in their private deployment; observed cache eviction around failures which exposes immediate re-introspection to IdP during the rotation window.
Reproducible in staging when intentionally removing 'sub' from introspection response; service returns 403 with 'principal not found' as expected.
resolution_and_workaround: Workaround applied (customer-side): temporarily increase token introspection cache TTL to 5 minutes to avoid repeated introspection calls during IdP key rotation window.

Platform workaround: added a temporary tolerant mapping in rbac-service to accept 'uid' claim as fallback when 'sub' is missing (canary patch deployed to their dedicated control plane). See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1428.

Longer term fix: implement robust missing-claim fallback and better error classification (distinguish transient introspection shape changes vs permanent rejections); scheduled backlog ticket INT-834 for full remediation.
Customer notified: advised to coordinate key rotations with a short overlap (old+new key acceptance) or pause rotations during peak traffic windows until fix rolled out.
